observations.text: SP, due to an abrupt power reduction combined with a late round-out during the transition from instrument flight to visual flight, did not maintain a smooth landing attitude and induced abrupt A/C attitude changes over the threshold. Touchdown developed approximately 1,600 feet beyond the projected touch down point, outside the 1,000 feet limit of standard 1. SP did not complete the landing without assistance, with the result that the IP directed the correction and executed part of the control inputs during the roll-out.

SP, due to continuation bias in maintaining the approach after the conditions had deteriorated below the briefed minima, did not recognize the runway environment positively and timely and delayed the transition from instrument flight to visual flight. The A/C was left displaced about 25 feet right of the center line at touchdown, beyond the 15 feet limit of standard 1. The landing was not completed without assistance, with the result that the IP took the controls to re-align the A/C during the landing roll.

SP transitioned from instrument flight to visual flight for landing within the desired standard for this Training Section, completing the landing after the IP's verbal prompts on airspeed and aim point. Touchdown was made 950 feet beyond the projected touch down point and 9 knots above the computed touchdown speed, both at the limits of standard 1, and recognition of the deviations was delayed. Marginal performance for the Training Section; earlier identification of the runway environment and independent correction of the aim point are expected to improve.

SP transitioned from instrument flight to visual flight after the ILS approach without abrupt A/C attitude changes and recognized the runway environment positively and timely. Minor deviations in aim point and lateral alignment produced a touchdown 700 feet from the projected touch down point and 8 feet left of the center line, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the transition from instrument flight to visual flight with accuracy and speed, holding a stabilized landing attitude without abrupt A/C attitude changes. The runway environment was identified positively and timely, with touchdown 300 feet from the projected touch down point, 3 feet from the center line and 3 knots above the computed touchdown speed. No verbal prompts from the IP were required at any point of the visual segment. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the transition from instrument flight to visual flight for landing with exceptional accuracy, holding the briefed final attitude without any abrupt A/C attitude changes. The runway environment was called immediately at break-out and touchdown was achieved within 100 feet of the projected touch down point, on the center line and at the computed touchdown speed. Deviations throughout the visual segment were negligible and performance was above the desired levels for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a high and fast profile carried unchanged through the transition from instrument flight to visual flight, did not adjust the aim point after break-out and floated through the flare with abrupt A/C attitude changes. Touchdown occurred about 1,800 feet beyond the projected touch down point and 14 knots above the computed touchdown speed, both outside the standard 1 limits. SP could not complete the landing without assistance, with the result that the IP took the controls and executed the go-around.

SP, due to an undesired aircraft state that was allowed to persist rather than being corrected, did not recognize the runway environment positively and timely after the GCA approach and continued an approach that was no longer within the landing parameters. Lateral displacement reached about 25 feet from the center line at touchdown, beyond the 15 feet limit of standard 1. The landing was not completed without assistance, with the result that the IP directed the correction and executed part of the control inputs during the roll-out.

SP, due to a late and non-standardized round-out during the transition from instrument flight to visual flight, did not arrest the descent rate at the correct height and allowed abrupt A/C attitude changes before touchdown. The A/C touched down 1,000 feet beyond the projected touch down point, at the limit of standard 1. The deviation was recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts, with delay.

SP, due to inadequate monitoring of airspeed during the approach, did not maintain the computed final airspeed through the transition from instrument flight to visual flight for landing. Touchdown speed was 10 knots above the computed value and lateral displacement reached 15 feet from the center line, both at the limits of standard 1. Recognition was delayed and the corrections were applied only after the IP's verbal prompts.

SP, due to a slightly late power reduction during the transition from instrument flight to visual flight, did not fully control the float in the flare, although the landing attitude was held without abrupt A/C attitude changes. Touchdown was made 800 feet beyond the projected touch down point and 7 knots above the computed touchdown speed. The errors were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on final, did not complete the cross-check of the aim point immediately after transitioning to visual flight for landing. The A/C touched down 9 feet left of the center line, between the standard 3 and standard 1 limits, without abrupt A/C attitude changes. The deviation was recognized and corrected during the roll-out in a timely manner and without IP's intervention.

SP transitioned from instrument flight to visual flight for landing within the desired standards, recognizing the runway environment positively and timely after the VOR/DME approach. Touchdown was 480 feet from the projected touch down point and 5 feet from the center line, at the outer edge of standard 3, and the aim point required two corrections during the flare. Marginal performance for the Training Section; greater consistency in aim point control through the visual segment is expected to improve.

SP executed the transition from instrument flight to visual flight for landing with exceptional accuracy, without any abrupt A/C attitude changes and with the runway environment identified immediately at break-out. Touchdown was achieved within 100 feet of the projected touch down point, on the center line and at the computed touchdown speed. Deviations throughout the visual segment were negligible, above the desired levels for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.
